summary_of_threads_started_this_week:
The newly developed **btc-safe** is a watch-only Bitcoin multisig coordinator that improves the security of multisignature transactions by allowing co-signers to independently sign transactions from separate devices, with the transaction only broadcasting after meeting a minimum approval threshold. This tool supports a variety of hardware wallets and software solutions and includes advanced security features such as TOTP two-factor authentication and role-specific account management, enhancing its functionality and user security. The complete codebase and a trial version on a signet test network are available for interested users and developers at [this GitHub link](https://github.com/tom2o17/btc-safe) and can [try it here](https://web-production-56752.up.railway.app). Source URL: https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/open-source-bitcoin-multisig-coordinator-shared-signing-queue-hardware-wallets-live-signet-demo/2957.

Bitcoin's evolution from a peer-to-peer electronic cash system to a reserve asset highlights significant shifts, including its increased accumulation by large entities and decreased use in everyday transactions. This transformation raises questions about Bitcoin's role in reinforcing economic disparities and suggests a potential departure from its democratizing ambitions, prompting discussions about alternative digital currencies like "humanitycoin" aimed at more egalitarian principles. Source URL: https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/from-peer-to-peer-cash-to-elite-settlement-layer-is-the-21m-cap-building-a-new-aristocracy/2959.

A new protocol integrates with Bitcoin Improvement Proposals to enhance the security of multiparty transactions using cryptographic techniques like elliptic curve cryptography and a discrete logarithm proof mechanism. This protocol ensures robust security in multiparty signing and remains compatible with existing Bitcoin protocols, contributing to the efficiency and interoperability within the Bitcoin ecosystem. Further cryptographic analysis and peer reviews are anticipated to solidify the protocol's security claims. Source URL: https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/silent-payments-for-multiparty-wallets/2960.

The release candidate for Bitcoin Core v32.0rc4 is now available, marking a significant step towards the final release of Bitcoin Core v32.0, assuming no critical issues arise during testing. Interested individuals can download the binaries and access preliminary release notes and a detailed testing guide through [Bitcoin Core's official website](https://bitcoincore.org/bin/bitcoin-core-32.0/test.rc4) and [GitHub](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/tree/v32.0rc4). Feedback from this testing phase is crucial for the upcoming official release. Source URL: https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/bitcoin-core-32-0rc4-is-now-available/2958.
